claim: The Drosophila visual system is an excellent paradigm to study how cellular diversity is generated.
source: The Drosophila visual system is an excellent paradigm to study how cellular diversity is generated.
evidence: This is a statement made in the abstract introducing the model system used in the study.

claim: Photoreceptors from the eye disc grow their axons into the optic lobe and secrete Hedgehog (Hh) to induce the lamina.
source: Photoreceptors from the eye disc grow their axons into the optic lobe and secrete Hedgehog (Hh) to induce the lamina, such that for every unit eye there is a corresponding lamina unit made up of post-mitotic precursors stacked into columns.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work in the field.

claim: For every unit eye there is a corresponding lamina unit made up of post-mitotic precursors stacked into columns.
source: Photoreceptors from the eye disc grow their axons into the optic lobe and secrete Hedgehog (Hh) to induce the lamina, such that for every unit eye there is a corresponding lamina unit made up of post-mitotic precursors stacked into columns.
evidence: This describes the structural organization of the lamina as established in the field.

claim: Each differentiated column contains five lamina neuron types (L1-L5).
source: Each differentiated column contains five lamina neuron types (L1-L5), making it the simplest neuropil in the optic lobe, yet how this diversity is generated was unknown.
evidence: This is a statement of known anatomical fact about the lamina structure.

claim: The lamina is the simplest neuropil in the optic lobe.
source: Each differentiated column contains five lamina neuron types (L1-L5), making it the simplest neuropil in the optic lobe, yet how this diversity is generated was unknown.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the complexity of different neuropils in the optic lobe.

claim: How lamina neuronal diversity is generated was unknown prior to this study.
source: Each differentiated column contains five lamina neuron types (L1-L5), making it the simplest neuropil in the optic lobe, yet how this diversity is generated was unknown.
evidence: This statement establishes the knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: Hh pathway activity is graded along the distal-proximal axis of lamina columns.
source: Here, we found that Hh pathway activity is graded along the distal-proximal axis of lamina columns, and further determined that this gradient in pathway activity arises from a gradient of Hh ligand.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The gradient in Hh pathway activity arises from a gradient of Hh ligand.
source: Here, we found that Hh pathway activity is graded along the distal-proximal axis of lamina columns, and further determined that this gradient in pathway activity arises from a gradient of Hh ligand.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Different thresholds of Hh pathway activity specify unique cell identities in the lamina.
source: These manipulations showed that different thresholds of activity specify unique cell identities, with more proximal cell types specified in response to progressively lower Hh levels.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figures 3-5.

claim: More proximal cell types are specified in response to progressively lower Hh levels.
source: These manipulations showed that different thresholds of activity specify unique cell identities, with more proximal cell types specified in response to progressively lower Hh levels.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data showing the relationship between Hh levels and cell identity.

claim: Hh acts as a morphogen to pattern the lamina.
source: Thus, our data establish that Hh acts as a morphogen to pattern the lamina.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on the experimental findings.

claim: This is the first report of a morphogen patterning neuronal fates during Drosophila nervous system development.
source: Although this is the first such report during Drosophila nervous system development, our work uncovers a remarkable similarity with the vertebrate neural tube, which is patterned by Sonic Hh.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding in the context of Drosophila neurobiology.

claim: The vertebrate neural tube is patterned by Sonic Hh.
source: Although this is the first such report during Drosophila nervous system development, our work uncovers a remarkable similarity with the vertebrate neural tube, which is patterned by Sonic Hh.
evidence: This is established knowledge about vertebrate neural development.

claim: There is a remarkable similarity between Drosophila lamina patterning and vertebrate neural tube patterning.
source: Although this is the first such report during Drosophila nervous system development, our work uncovers a remarkable similarity with the vertebrate neural tube, which is patterned by Sonic Hh.
evidence: This is a comparative conclusion drawn from the study's findings and existing knowledge.

claim: Differentiating neurons can regulate the neuronal diversity of their distant target fields through morphogen gradients.
source: Altogether, we show that differentiating neurons can regulate the neuronal diversity of their distant target fields through morphogen gradients.
evidence: This is a general principle derived from the study's findings about photoreceptor-derived Hh patterning the lamina.

claim: Invertebrates and vertebrates deploy common developmental strategies to diversify neural cell types.
source: Invertebrates and vertebrates deploy common developmental strategies to diversify neural cell types (Holguera and Desplan, 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The Drosophila visual system is composed of the compound eyes and optic lobes, which together contain ~200 neuronal cell types.
source: The Drosophila visual system is composed of the compound eyes and optic lobes, which together contain ~200 neuronal cell types (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Kurmangaliyev et al., 2020; Özel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about the composition of the visual system supported by citations.

claim: Each optic lobe is made up of four distinct neuropils: the lamina, medulla, lobula, and lobula plate.
source: Each optic lobe is made up of four distinct neuropils, the lamina, medulla, lobula, and lobula plate.
evidence: This is an anatomical description of the optic lobe structure.

claim: The medulla contains ~100 cell types.
source: With ~100 cell types, the medulla is the most diverse and complex (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Özel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about medulla complexity supported by citations.

claim: The medulla is the most diverse and complex neuropil in the optic lobe.
source: With ~100 cell types, the medulla is the most diverse and complex (Fischbach and Dittrich, 1989; Özel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a comparative statement about neuropil complexity supported by citations.

claim: The interplay between spatial patterning, temporal patterning, and Notch-mediated binary fate decisions accounts for medulla diversity.
source: Despite this, work in recent years has uncovered that the interplay between spatial patterning, temporal patterning, and Notch-mediated binary fate decisions accounts for medulla diversity (Bertet et al., 2014; Erclik et al., 2017; Gold and Brand, 2014; Konstantinides et al., 2021; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a summary of previous findings about medulla development supported by multiple citations.

claim: Much less is known about how diversity is generated in the lamina compared to the medulla.
source: In contrast, much less is known about how diversity is generated in the arguably simpler lamina, which contains only five neuronal cell types (L1-L5).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The lamina is the first neuropil to receive input from the photoreceptors.
source: The lamina is the first neuropil to receive input from the photoreceptors and its development is linked to and dependent on photoreceptor development (Huang et al., 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1996; Sugie et al., 2010; Umetsu et al., 2006; Yogev et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an anatomical and developmental fact supported by citations.

claim: Lamina development is linked to and dependent on photoreceptor development.
source: The lamina is the first neuropil to receive input from the photoreceptors and its development is linked to and dependent on photoreceptor development (Huang et al., 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1996; Sugie et al., 2010; Umetsu et al., 2006; Yogev et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about developmental dependency supported by citations.

claim: Photoreceptors are born progressively in the wake of a wave of differentiation that sweeps across the eye disc.
source: Photoreceptors are born progressively in the wake of a wave of differentiation that sweeps across the eye disc (Figure 1A; Roignant and Treisman, 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about photoreceptor development supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Two photoreceptor-derived signals, Hedgehog (Hh) and the EGF Spitz drive lamina development.
source: Two photoreceptor-derived signals, Hedgehog (Hh) and the EGF Spitz drive lamina development (Fernandes et al., 2017; Huang et al., 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1996; Sugie et al., 2010; Umetsu et al., 2006; Yogev et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about the signals driving lamina development supported by multiple citations.

claim: Hh signalling induces neuroepithelial cells to adopt lamina precursor cell (LPC) identity and express the lamina marker Dachshund (Dac).
source: Hh signalling induces neuroepithelial cells to adopt lamina precursor cell (LPC) identity and express the lamina marker Dachshund (Dac).
evidence: This is a statement about the role of Hh in LPC specification, which is established knowledge in the field.

claim: LPCs do not express classic neuroblast markers but are instead a distinct progenitor type.
source: LPCs do not express classic neuroblast markers but are instead a distinct progenitor type, which undergoes terminal divisions in response to Hh signalling (Apitz and Salecker, 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about LPC identity supported by citation.

claim: LPCs undergo terminal divisions in response to Hh signalling.
source: LPCs do not express classic neuroblast markers but are instead a distinct progenitor type, which undergoes terminal divisions in response to Hh signalling (Apitz and Salecker, 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about LPC behavior supported by citation.

claim: Hh signalling promotes LPC adhesion to photoreceptor axons, which facilitates their assembly into columns.
source: Finally, Hh signalling also promotes LPC adhesion to photoreceptor axons, which facilitates their assembly into columns (i.e. ensembles of stacked LPC cell bodies associated with photoreceptor axon bundles; Figure 1A and B; Huang and Kunes, 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1996; Sugie et al., 2010; Umetsu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about the role of Hh in column assembly supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Photoreceptor-derived EGF is required for LPCs to initiate neuronal differentiation.
source: Later in development, photoreceptor-derived EGF is required for LPCs to initiate neuronal differentiation (indicated by expression of the pan-neuronal marker Embryonic lethal abnormal vision [Elav]; Figure 1A and B; Huang et al., 1998; Yogev et al., 2010)
evidence: This is a statement about the role of EGF in lamina differentiation supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The communication between photoreceptors and LPCs for differentiation is indirect and involves a signalling relay through multiple glial populations.
source: however, this communication is indirect and involves a signalling relay through multiple glial populations, which ultimately induce lamina neuron differentiation through MAPK signalling (Figure 1A; Fernandes et al., 2017; Prasad et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of differentiation induction supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Glial populations ultimately induce lamina neuron differentiation through MAPK signalling.
source: however, this communication is indirect and involves a signalling relay through multiple glial populations, which ultimately induce lamina neuron differentiation through MAPK signalling (Figure 1A; Fernandes et al., 2017; Prasad et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanism of differentiation supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Lamina neuron identities are invariant and stereotyped according to their position along the distal-proximal axis of columns.
source: Lamina neuron identities are invariant and stereotyped according to their position along the distal-proximal axis of columns; LPCs in the distal-most positions of columns will differentiate into L2s, followed by L3s, then L1s, then L4s, and finally L5s are positioned at the proximal end of columns (Figure 1A and C; Pecot et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about the stereotyped positioning of lamina neurons supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A and C.

claim: LPCs in the distal-most positions of columns will differentiate into L2s, followed by L3s, then L1s, then L4s, and finally L5s are positioned at the proximal end of columns.
source: Lamina neuron identities are invariant and stereotyped according to their position along the distal-proximal axis of columns; LPCs in the distal-most positions of columns will differentiate into L2s, followed by L3s, then L1s, then L4s, and finally L5s are positioned at the proximal end of columns (Figure 1A and C; Pecot et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a detailed description of the spatial order of lamina neuron types supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A and C.

claim: Sloppy paired 2 (Slp2) alone labels L2s and L3s.
source: In addition, we can distinguish lamina neuron types using a combination of markers: Sloppy paired 2 (Slp2) alone labels L2s and L3s, Brain-specific homeobox (Bsh) alone labels L4s, Seven-up (Svp) together with Slp2 label L1s, and Slp2 together with Bsh label L5s (Figure 1A and C; Pecot et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about marker expression patterns supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A and C.

claim: Brain-specific homeobox (Bsh) alone labels L4s.
source: In addition, we can distinguish lamina neuron types using a combination of markers: Sloppy paired 2 (Slp2) alone labels L2s and L3s, Brain-specific homeobox (Bsh) alone labels L4s, Seven-up (Svp) together with Slp2 label L1s, and Slp2 together with Bsh label L5s (Figure 1A and C; Pecot et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about marker expression patterns supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A and C.

claim: Seven-up (Svp) together with Slp2 label L1s.
source: In addition, we can distinguish lamina neuron types using a combination of markers: Sloppy paired 2 (Slp2) alone labels L2s and L3s, Brain-specific homeobox (Bsh) alone labels L4s, Seven-up (Svp) together with Slp2 label L1s, and Slp2 together with Bsh label L5s (Figure 1A and C; Pecot et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about marker expression patterns supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A and C.

claim: Slp2 together with Bsh label L5s.
source: In addition, we can distinguish lamina neuron types using a combination of markers: Sloppy paired 2 (Slp2) alone labels L2s and L3s, Brain-specific homeobox (Bsh) alone labels L4s, Seven-up (Svp) together with Slp2 label L1s, and Slp2 together with Bsh label L5s (Figure 1A and C; Pecot et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about marker expression patterns supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A and C.

claim: The LPCs positioned between L4s and L5s do not differentiate but instead are fated to die by apoptosis.
source: The LPCs positioned between L4s and L5s do not differentiate but instead are fated to die by apoptosis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a statement about the fate of specific LPCs illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: MAPK signalling drives differentiation in the lamina indiscriminately for all neuronal types.
source: Given that MAPK signalling drives differentiation in the lamina indiscriminately for all neuronal types (Fernandes et al., 2017; Prasad et al., 2022), how these neurons acquire their individual identities has remained elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the role of MAPK signalling supported by citations.

claim: How lamina neurons acquire their individual identities has remained elusive.
source: Given that MAPK signalling drives differentiation in the lamina indiscriminately for all neuronal types (Fernandes et al., 2017; Prasad et al., 2022), how these neurons acquire their individual identities has remained elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: On UMAP visualizations, L1, L2, L3, and L4 neuronal clusters were closer to each other than they were to the L5 cluster.
source: As published previously, on uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) visualisations L1, L2, L3, and L4 neuronal clusters were closer to each other than they were to the L5 cluster (Özel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about scRNA-seq data analysis supported by citation.

claim: The LPC cluster was connected to differentiated neurons by two streams of cells: one leading to the L1-L4 clusters and the other leading to the L5 cluster.
source: The LPC cluster was connected to differentiated neurons by two streams of cells: one leading to the L1-L4 clusters and the other leading to the L5 cluster (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is a description of scRNA-seq data visualization shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Convergent streams in UMAP visualizations are thought to represent intermediate states between progenitors and differentiated cells.
source: such convergent streams are thought to represent intermediate states between progenitors and differentiated cells (Konstantinides et al., 2021; Özel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an interpretation of scRNA-seq data patterns supported by citations.

claim: L3 neurons express earmuff (erm).
source: Consistent with previous reports, scRNAseq analysis showed that L3 and L4 neurons expressed earmuff (erm) and apterous (ap), respectively (Tan et al., 2015; Ting et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement about marker expression supported by citations and scRNA-seq data.

claim: L4 neurons express apterous (ap).
source: Consistent with previous reports, scRNAseq analysis showed that L3 and L4 neurons expressed earmuff (erm) and apterous (ap), respectively (Tan et al., 2015; Ting et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement about marker expression supported by citations and scRNA-seq data.

claim: Reduced ocelli (rdo) is expressed at high levels in L2 neurons and at lower levels and more sporadically in L3 neurons.
source: In addition, we found that reduced ocelli (rdo) was expressed at high levels in L2 neurons and at lower levels and more sporadically in L3 neurons
evidence: This is a finding from scRNA-seq data analysis.

claim: L1 neurons express Vesicular glutamate transporter (VGlut) specifically.
source: that L1 neurons expressed Vesicular glutamate transporter (VGlut) specifically
evidence: This is a finding from scRNA-seq data analysis.

claim: L5 neurons express high levels of defective proboscis extension response 8 (dpr8).
source: and that L5 and L3 neurons expressed high and low levels of defective proboscis extension response 8 (dpr8), respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–F).
evidence: This is a finding from scRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–F.

claim: L3 neurons express low levels of defective proboscis extension response 8 (dpr8).
source: and that L5 and L3 neurons expressed high and low levels of defective proboscis extension response 8 (dpr8), respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–F).
evidence: This is a finding from scRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–F.

claim: Several well-established Hh signalling targets were expressed at higher levels in the L1-L4 stream compared with the L5 stream.
source: Surprisingly, comparing gene expression between the two streams connecting undifferentiated LPCs with L1-L4s and L5s, indicated that several well-established Hh signalling targets were expressed at higher levels in the L1-L4 stream compared with the L5 stream, suggesting that L5 precursors experience lower Hh signalling than other lamina precursors.
evidence: This is a finding from scRNA-seq data analysis.

claim: L5 precursors experience lower Hh signalling than other lamina precursors.
source: Surprisingly, comparing gene expression between the two streams connecting undifferentiated LPCs with L1-L4s and L5s, indicated that several well-established Hh signalling targets were expressed at higher levels in the L1-L4 stream compared with the L5 stream, suggesting that L5 precursors experience lower Hh signalling than other lamina precursors.
evidence: This is an inference from scRNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Patched (ptc) is a direct transcriptional target of Hh signalling.
source: These included the direct transcriptional target patched (ptc), as well as single-minded (sim), rhomboid (rho), and Zinc finger homeodomain 1 (zfh1) (Figure 1E–H; Albert et al., 2018; Biehs et al., 2010; Chen and Struhl, 1996; Umetsu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about ptc as a Hh target supported by citations and shown in Figure 1E–H.

claim: Single-minded (sim), rhomboid (rho), and Zinc finger homeodomain 1 (zfh1) are Hh signalling targets.
source: These included the direct transcriptional target patched (ptc), as well as single-minded (sim), rhomboid (rho), and Zinc finger homeodomain 1 (zfh1) (Figure 1E–H; Albert et al., 2018; Biehs et al., 2010; Chen and Struhl, 1996; Umetsu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about Hh targets supported by citations and shown in Figure 1E–H.

claim: In young columns prior to neuronal differentiation, there is a gradient of ptc-lacZ expression, which is highest in the distal lamina and decreases along the distal-proximal axis.
source: Importantly, in young columns prior to neuronal differentiation, we observed a gradient of ptc-lacZ expression, which was highest in the distal lamina and decreased along the distal-proximal axis (Figure 1K; one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1K with statistical analysis.

claim: There is a gradient of Hh signalling activity in lamina columns prior to neuronal differentiation.
source: Thus, we observed that the direct Hh signalling target, ptc, was graded along the distal to proximal length of the youngest column, indicating that there is a gradient of Hh signalling activity in lamina columns prior to neuronal differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ptc-lacZ expression data.

claim: Hh::GFP is present in a distal to proximal gradient in the lamina.
source: We measured Hh::GFP MFI as a function of distal-proximal distance for the youngest lamina column (see Materials and methods section) and observed a gradient polarised from high to low from the distal to proximal ends of columns (Figure 2B–C; N=10).
evidence: This is a primary finding from live imaging data shown in Figure 2B–C.

claim: Hh ligand is present in a distal to proximal gradient in the lamina, consistent with the gradient in Hh pathway activity along lamina columns.
source: Nonetheless, these data indicate that Hh ligand is present in a distal to proximal gradient in the lamina, consistent with the gradient in Hh pathway activity along lamina columns and suggest that ligand availability is responsible for the activity gradient.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Hh::GFP distribution data.

claim: Ligand availability is responsible for the Hh pathway activity gradient.
source: Nonetheless, these data indicate that Hh ligand is present in a distal to proximal gradient in the lamina, consistent with the gradient in Hh pathway activity along lamina columns and suggest that ligand availability is responsible for the activity gradient.
evidence: This is an inference from the correlation between ligand distribution and pathway activity.

claim: Hh signalling triggers the early steps of lamina development, including promoting early lamina marker expressions such as dac and sim.
source: Hh signalling is known to trigger the early steps of lamina development, including promoting early lamina marker expressions such as dac and sim, as well as promoting terminal LPC divisions and column assembly (Huang and Kunes, 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1996; Sugie et al., 2010; Umetsu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about the known roles of Hh signalling supported by citations.

claim: Hh signalling promotes terminal LPC divisions and column assembly.
source: Hh signalling is known to trigger the early steps of lamina development, including promoting early lamina marker expressions such as dac and sim, as well as promoting terminal LPC divisions and column assembly (Huang and Kunes, 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1996; Sugie et al., 2010; Umetsu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about the known roles of Hh signalling supported by citations.

claim: No role for Hh in lamina neuron specification or differentiation has been identified prior to this study.
source: However, no role for Hh in lamina neuron specification or differentiation has been identified thus far.
evidence: This is a statement about the knowledge gap in the field.

claim: A gradient of Shh signalling specifies ventral progenitor identities in the vertebrate neural tube.
source: In the vertebrate neural tube, a gradient of Shh signalling specifies ventral progenitor identities (Placzek and Briscoe, 2018)
evidence: This is a statement about vertebrate neural development supported by citation.

claim: Increasing Hh signalling maximally in the lamina results in distal neuron specification (mixed L2 and L3) at the expense of L1, L4, and L5 specifications.
source: Thus, increasing Hh signalling maximally in the lamina resulted in distal neuron specification (mixed L2 and L3) at the expense of L1, L4, and L5 specifications.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the ptc mutant clone experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: ptc mutant clones never contained L5s, L4s, or L1s but instead only contained neurons singly positive for Slp2, indicative of L2/L3 identity.
source: The ptc mutant clones never contained L5s (Slp2 and Bsh co-expressing cells), L4s (Bsh-only expressing cells), or L1s (Svp and Slp2 co-expressing cells) but instead only contained neurons singly positive for Slp2, indicative of L2/L3 identity (Figure 3A–B; 17/17 clones from 15 optic lobes; fully penetrant phenotype).
evidence: This is a primary finding from MARCM clone experiments shown in Figure 3A–B.

claim: ptc mutant clones in the proximal lamina contained mixed rdo and erm expression, indicating that both L2 and L3 neurons were present.
source: To determine the precise identity of these neurons (L2 or L3), we examined the expression of rdo and erm by HCR in ptc mutant clones in the proximal lamina and found mixed rdo and erm expression (Figure 3C–D; N=15/15 clones), which indicated that both L2 and L3 neurons were present in the clones.
evidence: This is a primary finding from HCR experiments shown in Figure 3C–D.

claim: When Hh pathway activity is blocked completely in clones mutant for smoothened (smo), no Dac-expressing LPCs are recovered.
source: When we blocked Hh pathway activity completely in clones mutant for smoothened (smo), we did not recover any Dac-expressing LPCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A; N=15/15 clones; fully penetrant phenotype), consistent with previous reports (Huang and Kunes, 1998).
evidence: This is a finding from smo mutant clone experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, consistent with previous reports.

claim: Expressing Cirep in LPCs led to a 2.8-fold increase in the proportion of L5s relative to controls.
source: Expressing Cirep in LPCs led to a 2.8-fold increase in the proportion of Bsh and Slp2 double-positive L5s relative to controls, while the proportion of other lamina neuron subtypes was reduced relative to controls (Figure 3E, F and H–L and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F; one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; p-values <0.001; N=10).
evidence: This is a primary finding from genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 3 with statistical analysis.

claim: Expressing Cirep caused L5s to be distributed along the entire distal-proximal lengths of columns instead of being restricted to a single row in the proximal lamina.
source: Moreover, whereas in control laminas L5s were only observed as a single row in the proximal lamina, expressing Cirep caused Bsh and Slp2 double-positive L5s to be distributed along the entire distal-proximal lengths of columns (Figure 3F, N=10).
evidence: This is a primary finding from genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Knocking down Ci in the lamina by RNA interference resulted in ectopic L5s (2.4-fold increase relative to controls).
source: Similarly, knocking down Ci in the lamina by RNA interference (CiRNAi) (Figure 3G; N=9) resulted in ectopic L5s (2.4-fold increase relative to controls, one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; p<0.0001)
evidence: This is a primary finding from RNAi experiments shown in Figure 3G with statistical analysis.

claim: Knocking down Ci in the lamina resulted in a reduction in the proportion of L2-L3s and L4 lamina neurons relative to controls.
source: and a reduction in the proportion of L2-L3s and L4 lamina neurons relative to controls (Figure 3H–L, one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; pL2-L3<0.0001 and pL4<0.0001; see Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F for raw values).
evidence: This is a primary finding from RNAi experiments shown in Figure 3 with statistical analysis.

claim: Decreasing Hh signalling autonomously within LPCs is sufficient to induce the most proximal cell identity (L5s) throughout the distal-proximal lengths of columns and at the expense of other neuronal types.
source: Thus, decreasing Hh signalling autonomously within LPCs was sufficient to induce the most proximal cell identity (L5s), throughout the distal-proximal lengths of columns and at the expense of other neuronal types.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the Cirep and CiRNAi experiments.

claim: Disrupting Hh signalling activity cell autonomously to either high or low extremes specifies LPCs with either the most distal or proximal lamina neuron identities, respectively.
source: In summary, disrupting Hh signalling activity cell autonomously to either high or low extremes specified LPCs with either the most distal or proximal lamina neuron identities, respectively.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the cell-autonomous manipulation experiments.

claim: Strong inhibition of Hh signalling (laminats >Cirep at 29°C) led to a 2.2-fold increase relative to controls in the proportion of the lamina that co-expressed dpr8 and bsh (L5s) at the expense of other markers.
source: Strong inhibition of Hh signalling (laminats >Cirep at 29°C) led to a 2.2-fold increase relative to controls in the proportion of the lamina that co-expressed dpr8 and bsh (i.e. L5s) at the expense of other markers (Figure 4A–F and J–N; Ndpr8+bsh=8; one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; pdpr8+bsh<0.0001).
evidence: This is a primary finding from temperature-controlled genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 4 with statistical analysis.

claim: Milder inhibition of Hh signalling (laminats >Cirep at 25°C) led to a 2.5-fold increase relative to controls in the proportion of the lamina that expressed VGlut (L1s).
source: In contrast, milder inhibition of Hh signalling (laminats >Cirep at 25°C) led to a 2.5-fold increase relative to controls in the proportion of the lamina that expressed VGlut (i.e. L1s) and a 1.9-fold increase relative to controls in the proportion of the lamina that expressed ap (i.e. L4s), at the expense of rdo expressing (erm-negative) L2s (Figure 4A–C– and J–N; one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; pVGlut<0.0001; pap<0.01).
evidence: This is a primary finding from temperature-controlled genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 4 with statistical analysis.

claim: Milder inhibition of Hh signalling (laminats >Cirep at 25°C) led to a 1.9-fold increase relative to controls in the proportion of the lamina that expressed ap (L4s).
source: In contrast, milder inhibition of Hh signalling (laminats >Cirep at 25°C) led to a 2.5-fold increase relative to controls in the proportion of the lamina that expressed VGlut (i.e. L1s) and a 1.9-fold increase relative to controls in the proportion of the lamina that expressed ap (i.e. L4s), at the expense of rdo expressing (erm-negative) L2s (Figure 4A–C– and J–N; one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; pVGlut<0.0001; pap<0.01).
evidence: This is a primary finding from temperature-controlled genetic manipulation experiments shown in Figure 4 with statistical analysis.

claim: Intermediate neuron identities (L1s and L4s) are favoured when Hh signalling is tuned to intermediate levels.
source: Thus, intermediate neuron identities (L1s and L4s) were favoured when we tuned Hh signalling to intermediate levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the temperature-controlled Cirep experiments.

claim: Progressively reducing Hh levels results in progressively more proximal identities.
source: We predicted that, if Hh was acting as a morphogen, progressively reducing Hh levels should result in progressively more proximal identities.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the morphogen hypothesis that was tested experimentally.

claim: Fewer photoreceptors and lamina neurons are recovered with increasing lengths of temperature shifts in hhts2 mutants.
source: Consistent with the known role of Hh signalling in photoreceptor and early lamina development (Huang and Kunes, 1996), we recovered fewer and fewer photoreceptors and lamina neurons with increasing lengths of temperature shifts (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-J), with no LPCs or lamina neurons recovered for the 45-hr and 72-hr temperature shifts (Figure 5F and G; Huang and Kunes, 1996).
evidence: This is a finding from hhts2 temperature shift experiments shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1, consistent with previous reports.

claim: The proportion of L2-L3s decreased as the availability of functional Hh was titrated to lower levels in hhts2 temperature shift experiments.
source: We found that the proportion of L2-L3s (Slp2 single-positive neurons) decreased as the availability of functional Hh was titrated to lower and lower levels, whereas the proportion of L5s (Slp2 and Bsh double-positive neurons) increased (Figure 5A–E; quantified in Figure 5I–L; one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; p-values <0.05).
evidence: This is a primary finding from hhts2 temperature shift experiments shown in Figure 5 with statistical analysis.

claim: The proportion of L5s increased as the availability of functional Hh was titrated to lower levels in hhts2 temperature shift experiments.
source: We found that the proportion of L2-L3s (Slp2 single-positive neurons) decreased as the availability of functional Hh was titrated to lower and lower levels, whereas the proportion of L5s (Slp2 and Bsh double-positive neurons) increased (Figure 5A–E; quantified in Figure 5I–L; one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; p-values <0.05).
evidence: This is a primary finding from hhts2 temperature shift experiments shown in Figure 5 with statistical analysis.

claim: The proportion of L1s increased only for the 6-hr temperature shift in hhts2 experiments.
source: Importantly, the proportion of L1s (Slp2 and Svp double-positive neurons) increased only for the 6-hr temperature shift.
evidence: This is a primary finding from hhts2 temperature shift experiments.

claim: L1 neurons, which normally occupy intermediate lamina column positions, are favoured at the expense of distal neuron types at intermediate thresholds of Hh pathway activity.
source: Thus, L1 neurons, which normally occupy intermediate lamina column positions were favoured at the expense of distal neuron types at intermediate thresholds of Hh pathway activity (Figure 5C and J; one-way ANOVA with Dunn's multiple comparisons test; p-values <0.05).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the hhts2 temperature shift experiments shown in Figure 5 with statistical analysis.

claim: Under hhts2 temperature shift conditions, L1s and L5s are no longer confined to their normal positions within lamina columns but are observed throughout.
source: Notably, under these conditions, L1s and L5s were no longer confined to their normal positions within lamina columns but were observed throughout (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This is a finding from hhts2 temperature shift experiments shown in Figure 5A–D.

claim: The data establish that Hh acts as a morphogen to diversify lamina neuron types.
source: Altogether our data establish that Hh acts as a morphogen to diversify lamina neuron types.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on all the experimental findings.

claim: Photoreceptors are the sole source of Hh to the optic lobes during lamina development.
source: Others have reported previously that photoreceptors are the sole source of Hh to the optic lobes during lamina development (Huang and Kunes, 1996).
evidence: This is a statement about the source of Hh supported by citation to previous work.

claim: hh-lacZ (hhP30) expression is restricted to photoreceptors in the eye disc and absent from the optic lobes, except for a few sparse cells near the central brain.
source: We corroborated these results using an enhancer trap in the hh locus (hh-lacZ; hhP30), which showed that β-Gal expression was restricted to photoreceptors in the eye disc and absent from the optic lobes, except for a few sparse cells near the central brain (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from hh-lacZ reporter expression analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Hh secreted by developing photoreceptors is required to drive morphogenetic furrow progression and continued photoreceptor development in the eye disc.
source: Hh secreted by developing photoreceptors is required to drive morphogenetic furrow progression and continued photoreceptor development in the eye disc (Greenwood and Struhl, 1999; Treisman, 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about the role of Hh in eye development supported by citations.

claim: Removing hh expression completely in the eye disc blocks both photoreceptor development and lamina development.
source: Consequently, removing hh expression completely in the eye disc has been shown to block both photoreceptor development (Greenwood and Struhl, 1999; Treisman, 2013) and lamina development, due to its early role in inducing LPCs (Huang and Kunes, 1998; Huang and Kunes, 1996).
evidence: This is a statement about the consequences of removing hh supported by citations.

claim: Partially knocking down Hh in photoreceptors using GMR-Gal4 and RNAi does not noticeably affect lamina size.
source: Under these conditions, lamina size was not noticeably affected, indicative of a mild knockdown (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from photoreceptor-specific Hh knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Partially knocking down Hh expression in photoreceptors led to a 1.2-fold increase in L1 neurons relative to controls.
source: When we evaluated lamina neuron-type identities, we found that Slp2 and Svp expressing cells (L1s) increased by 1.2-fold relative to controls (Figure 6C; Mann-Whitney U test; p<0.001; N=10), consistent with more LPCs experiencing intermediate Hh signalling activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding from photoreceptor-specific Hh knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6C with statistical analysis.

claim: When Hh is partially knocked down in photoreceptors, L1 neurons are no longer restricted to a single row at intermediate positions in columns but are recovered in more distal positions.
source: Importantly, L1 neurons were no longer restricted to a single row at intermediate positions in columns but instead were recovered in more distal positions (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a finding from photoreceptor-specific Hh knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Partially knocking down Hh expression in photoreceptors disrupts lamina neuron patterning in favour of more intermediate cell identities (L1s).
source: Thus, partially knocking down Hh expression in photoreceptors disrupted lamina neuron patterning in favour of more intermediate cell identities (L1s), consistent with mildly decreasing Hh signalling to more intermediate levels in the lamina.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the photoreceptor-specific Hh knockdown experiments.

claim: This work uncovers a previously unknown role for Hh as a morphogen that specifies lamina neuron identities.
source: Here, we uncovered a previously unknown role for Hh as a morphogen that specifies lamina neuron identities, thus revealing yet another layer of dependence of lamina development on photoreceptor-derived signals.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's main finding.

claim: Lamina development has yet another layer of dependence on photoreceptor-derived signals.
source: Here, we uncovered a previously unknown role for Hh as a morphogen that specifies lamina neuron identities, thus revealing yet another layer of dependence of lamina development on photoreceptor-derived signals.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the relationship between photoreceptors and lamina development.

claim: A mix of L2 and L3 identities are specified when Hh signalling is activated to maximum physiological levels.
source: Intriguingly, a mix of L2 and L3 identities were specified when Hh signalling was activated to maximum physiological levels (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the ptc mutant clone experiments shown in Figure 3D.

claim: In addition to high Hh signalling levels, additional signals are required to further differentiate L2 from L3 identities.
source: This suggests that in addition to high Hh signalling levels, additional signals are required to further differentiate L2 from L3 identities.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that both L2 and L3 are specified at high Hh levels.

claim: Morphogen patterning of neuronal fates is widespread in vertebrates.
source: It highlights the remarkable evolutionary conservation of this developmental strategy, which is widespread in vertebrates (Placzek and Briscoe, 2018; Sagner and Briscoe, 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about vertebrate development supported by citations.

claim: Axonal trafficking of Hh is regulated by an evolutionarily conserved motif in its cleaved C-terminal domain.
source: Axonal trafficking of Hh was shown to be regulated by an evolutionarily conserved motif in its cleaved C-terminal domain (Chu et al., 2006; Daniele et al., 2017)
evidence: This is a statement about Hh trafficking supported by citations.

claim: Disruption of the C-terminal motif in Hh affected neuronal diversity in the lamina specifically.
source: disruption of which affected neuronal diversity in the lamina specifically (Chu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about the effects of disrupting Hh trafficking supported by citation.

claim: Axonal trafficking may play a role in establishing the Hh gradient in the lamina.
source: This indicates that axonal trafficking may play a role in establishing the Hh gradient; however, more work is required to uncover the exact molecular mechanisms involved.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of gradient formation based on previous findings.

claim: It is unexpected that neurons (photoreceptors) define the neuronal diversity of their target field.
source: It is unexpected that neurons, here photoreceptors, define the neuronal diversity of their target field, and raises the possibility that neurons in other contexts could also be patterning their target fields during development through morphogen gradients.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty and implications of the finding.

claim: Neurons in other contexts could be patterning their target fields during development through morphogen gradients.
source: It is unexpected that neurons, here photoreceptors, define the neuronal diversity of their target field, and raises the possibility that neurons in other contexts could also be patterning their target fields during development through morphogen gradients.
evidence: This is a speculation about broader implications of the finding.

claim: Many vertebrate neuronal types express Shh.
source: Indeed, many vertebrate neuronal types express Shh (Dakubo et al., 2003; Farmer et al., 2016; Garcia et al., 2010; Gonzalez-Reyes et al., 2012; Harwell et al., 2012; Petralia et al., 2011; Wallace, 1999)
evidence: This is a statement about Shh expression in vertebrate neurons supported by multiple citations.

claim: The ability of vertebrate neurons to generate instructive gradients to pattern distant neural fields has not been determined.
source: however, their ability to generate instructive gradients to pattern distant neural fields has not been determined thus far.
evidence: This is a statement about a knowledge gap in vertebrate neurobiology.

claim: Hh::GFP expressed under the control of endogenous enhancers of the hh locus rescues a hh amorph.
source: This transgene was previously reported to rescue a hh amorph, indicating that it is a functional hh allele (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the functionality of the Hh::GFP transgene supported by citation.

claim: Higher levels of Hh::GFP are observed in younger photoreceptor cell bodies compared to older photoreceptor cell bodies in the eye disc.
source: We first used immunohistochemistry (IHC) to detect Hh::GFP and observed higher levels in younger photoreceptor cell bodies compared to older photoreceptor cell bodies in the eye disc, consistent with previous reports (Figure 2A, A'; Huang and Kunes, 1996).
evidence: This is a finding from IHC experiments shown in Figure 2A, A' that is consistent with previous reports.

claim: Hh::GFP is observed in photoreceptor axons in the optic stalk but very little signal is observed in photoreceptor axons in the lamina by IHC.
source: We also observed Hh::GFP in photoreceptor axons in the optic stalk but observed very little signal in photoreceptor axons in the lamina (Figure 2A, A'; N=18).
evidence: This is a finding from IHC experiments shown in Figure 2A, A'.

claim: Secreted proteins can be particularly sensitive to fixation and washes during IHC.
source: Secreted proteins can be particularly sensitive to fixation and washes during IHC, therefore to avoid any confounding artefacts potentially caused by IHC, we visualised Hh::GFP live in cultured brain explants (Bostock et al., 2020; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a statement about a technical consideration in the experimental approach.

claim: The measurements of Hh::GFP MFI do not distinguish between intracellular and extracellular Hh::GFP, but represent total Hh::GFP.
source: These measurements do not distinguish between intracellular and extracellular Hh::GFP, but instead, represent total Hh::GFP.
evidence: This is a clarification about the nature of the measurements.

claim: ptc-lacZ expression eventually decreases along the young to old axis for each of the six distal-proximal cell positions.
source: Consistent with the transcriptomic data where ptc expression was lowest in older maturing neurons (Figure 1E), ptc-lacZ expression eventually decreased along the young to old axis for each of the six (distal-proximal) cell positions (Figure 1I and J; N=10).
evidence: This is a finding from ptc-lacZ reporter analysis shown in Figure 1I and J that is consistent with scRNA-seq data.

claim: L5s and excess LPCs begin with and maintain the lowest levels of ptc-lacZ (β-Gal) expression over time.
source: The L5s and the excess LPCs began with and maintained the lowest levels of β-Gal expression over time.
evidence: This is a finding from ptc-lacZ reporter analysis.

claim: R27G05-Gal4 drives expression in Dac-expressing LPCs exiting the posterior lamina furrow.
source: Therefore, to reduce Hh pathway activity partially, we used a lamina-specific driver (R27G05-Gal4), which drives expression in Dac-expressing LPCs exiting the posterior lamina furrow (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is a description of the expression pattern of the Gal4 driver shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.
